| `content`            | `{ tabs?: Array<{widgetId?: string, widgetIds?: string[], label?: string, icon?: string, count?: number, countField?: string, countFrom?: ('widget'&#124;{register: string, schema: string, filter?: object}&#124;{endpoint: string, field?: string}), overflow?: boolean, default?: boolean, columns?: number, layout?: Array<{widgetId: string, gridWidth: number}>}>, ariaLabel?: string, maxVisibleTabs?: number, hideEmpty?: boolean, moreLabel?: string, variant?: ('line'&#124;'segmented') }` |          | `\{\}`          | The widget's config: `{ tabs, ariaLabel }`. `tabs[]` entries are `{ widgetId, label?, icon?, count?, countField?, overflow? }`. `label` and `icon` fall back to the referenced widget's own title and icon. `count` is a number shown after the label; `countField` reads it off the record instead (a list counts its items). `countFrom` counts a list on the server: `"widget"` counts the child widget's own list (`content.register`, `schema`, `filter`, tokens such as `@objectId` resolved), an object `{ register, schema, filter? }` names the list, and `{ endpoint, field? }` counts the list (or reads the number) an endpoint answers with, `@objectId` resolved; `count` and `countField` win over it. `overflow: true` lists the tab under "More". A tab with `widgetIds` can lay them out in a grid instead of one under the other: `columns: 4` gives each a quarter of the row, and `layout: [{ widgetId, gridWidth }]` sets a width (of 12) per widget, as the page grid does. Widgets wrap onto the next row. A tab with `default: true` is the one the strip opens on, unless a route hash names another tab or the marked tab sits under "More". `maxVisibleTabs` caps the strip: later tabs go under "More" (in the board look: into the Actions menu, with History kept in the strip). `hideEmpty: true` moves a tab whose count is 0 there too. `moreLabel` names that menu. `variant: "segmented"` draws the strip as a pill switch (CnTabs' segmented variant); `line` is the default. |
